Loqui is built so that dictation works without an account, a server or a key. This page describes exactly what leaves your phone and when.

Loqui records only while you dictate. The microphone service starts on a tap and stops at the end of the sentence, or as soon as you tap again. Nothing is recorded in the background and no audio is ever written to a file.
On-device recognition is the default and needs no key: audio is processed on your phone and never uploaded. Loqui runs no server of its own.
If you switch recognition to cloud, the audio for that dictation goes from your phone straight to the provider you chose, with your own key, under that provider’s terms. Nothing is routed through us.

Clean-up is off by default. On-device clean-up fixes punctuation on your phone without a network call. Cloud clean-up sends the transcript text — never audio — to your provider with your own key, and only while the toggle is on.
There is no transcript history, no analytics SDK and no crash-reporting SDK. Logs record counts and durations only — never the words you spoke — and release builds ship no debug logging.

Provider keys are encrypted with a key held in the Android Keystore. They never appear in logs, never ship in the APK and are only sent to the endpoint you selected. Remove a key at any time from the home screen.

The accessibility service has one job: pasting the transcript into the field you have focused. It does not read the screen for anything else, does not observe your typing and stores nothing. Without it, transcripts go to the clipboard instead.
Speech models are downloaded at runtime, never bundled in the APK. A model is only offered after its license and checksum have been recorded, and nothing is downloaded without your tap.

Microphone records, notifications show the required foreground notification, display-over-other-apps draws the bubble, battery exemption keeps it alive, accessibility inserts. Each is revocable in system settings and each has a fallback.
The policy ships with the build, so you always read the version that matches the app you installed. A hosted copy of this text is required for the Play Store listing before release.
Android requires your permission before any app can use the accessibility API. Loqui uses it for one thing: inserting the transcript you just dictated into the text field you have focused.

• Reads only the focused text field, at the moment of insertion
• Never reads other screens, keystrokes or passwords
• Stores nothing and runs no background monitoring
• Optional — without it the transcript is copied to the clipboard
